sentences.text:
Apsrtc vs Rajaputhra Vijaya Singh on 21 June, 2023
Author: Lalitha Kanneganti

Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2710 of 2008
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award dated 08.12.2006 in O.P.No.862 of 2003 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VI- Additional District Judge, Mahabubnagar, the claimant-RTC has filed MACMA No.2710 of 2008.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-VI- Additional District Judge, Mahabubnagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard learned Standing Counsel for RTC and learned counsel for respondents, perused the entire material on record.
3. The brief facts are that on 02.12.1997 at about 6.30 hours, the driver of the lorry was driving the lorry to got to Nagarkurnool from Achampet.

When the said lorry reached Kurvoni Gutta in the limits of Rakonda village on B.T. road and at the same time R.T.C bus belonging to Achampet R.T.C depot, which was coming in opposite direction from Nagarkurnool side drove in a rash and negligent manner in high speed and dashed against the lorry.
The lorry was heavily damaged.
He filed OP., claiming compensation of 2,50,000/- for the damage of lorry.

Respondent No.2-Insurance Company filed counter denying the manner of accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the crime vehicle and the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant and the amount that was spent by him for his treatment.
It is stated that the claim is excessive and exorbitant.
5. The Court below on analyzing the oral and documentary evidence has granted compensation of Rs.68,004/- with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant-RTC submits that the driver of the RTC bus was acquitted in the criminal case which shows that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, as such, the Tribunal have granted the compensation.
He further submits that the Court below failed to consider the RW.1 and appreciate the evidence on behalf of the claimant that there is negligence on the part of the bus driver.
However, it is stated that the Tribunal failed to consider contributory negligence on the part of the lorry driver LK, J MACMA_2710_2008 as the accident occurred due to the head on collusion.

The Court below ought not to have granted the compensation under the head of loss of income which is out of scope of the act and the Court below without any Apsrtc vs Rajaputhra Vijaya Singh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132935106/
1 basis and contrary to law has granted the said compensation.
7.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the Court below having considered all the aspects and the law laid down by this Court has granted compensation.
It is submitted that the RTC failed to make out any grounds seeking interference with the award passed by the Court below.

The Court below has observed that in the said case, the RTC bus driver was acquitted by the criminal Court by giving benefit of doubt and the burden of proof in a criminal case is beyond reasonable doubt.
Whereas in this case it is preponderance of probability.

This case cannot be equated with the criminal case just because the driver of the vehicle was acquitted, that itself cannot be a ground for the appellant-RTC to contend that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the RTC bus.

LK, J MACMA_2710_2008 8. Coming to the compensation that was granted by the Court below, it has rightly considered the legal position and granted the compensation.
9.
In that view of the mater, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the award passed by Tribunal.
10. In the result, the Motor Accident Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed.

Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
___________________________ LALITHA KANNEGANTI, J Date: 21.06.2023 prat Apsrtc vs Rajaputhra Vijaya Singh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132935106/
